sec: Wilson's presentations, jaundice types, histology and cristae

items.q: Why does fulminant hepatic failure in Wilson's disease characteristically exhibit a depressed serum Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP)?
opts: Massive copper release displaces zinc, an essential co-factor required for the active site of alkaline phosphatase
Copper toxicity causes selective transcriptional down-regulation of osteoblastic genes
Circulating copper directly binds to and inactivates the canalicular MRP-2 transporter
Alkaline phosphatase is preferentially filtered and lost in urine
items.exp: The text explains low ALP as: '(Zn2+ & Cu2+ competing for ALP)' where excess copper displaces zinc. (Book p1014)

items.q: What is the typical presentation of chronic Wilson's disease before overt cirrhosis?
opts: Young asymptomatic patient with fatigue and mild transaminase elevation (<150 U/L) where ALT > AST
Severe right upper quadrant pain with transaminases >2000 U/L
Isolated massive ascites without any constitutional symptoms
Rapid onset of chorea within weeks of first symptom
items.exp: Chronic presentation has no specific symptoms: 'Fatigue + enzymes (<150 U/L) ALT > AST ... Young asymptomatic pt. with rise in serum enzymes'. (Book p1014)

items.q: Fill up: On abdominal ultrasound, cirrhotic Wilson's disease characteristically displays a mixed cirrhosis pattern with ______ nodules predominating over micronodules.
Which metabolic liver disease carries the 'maximum jaundice tendency' among all hepatic disorders?
items.exp: The header explicitly highlights: 'Jaundice in Wilson's disease : maximum jaundice tendency'. (Book p1014)

items.q: Match each type of jaundice observed in Wilson's disease with its specific etiology — 1) Pre-hepatic / Hemolytic 2) Hepatic 3) Post-hepatic / Obstructive … A) Acute and chronic hepatocellular necrosis (disease proper) B) Gallstones and cholestasis C) Coombs-negative hemolytic anemia in fulminant failure
items.exp: Wilson's produces all 3 jaundice types: pre-hepatic via Coombs-negative hemolysis, hepatic via disease proper, and post-hepatic via gallstones/cholestasis. (Book p1014)

items.q: What ultrastructural mitochondrial abnormality on electron microscopy is characteristic of Wilson's disease?
opts: Tennis racquet appearance due to dilatation of the tips of mitochondrial cristae
Concentric whorls of smooth endoplasmic reticulum (fingerprint bodies)
Giant paracrystalline inclusions inside the mitochondrial matrix
Disruption of the outer mitochondrial membrane with cytochrome c leakage
items.exp: Electron microscopy shows 'Tennis racquet appearance (mitochondria involved) d/t dilatation of tips of cristae.' (Book p1014)

items.q: Fill up: On liver histology, hepatocytes in Wilson's disease characteristically exhibit ______ nuclei due to glycogenic degeneration.
items.exp: Histopathology lists: 'Glycogenated nucleus inside hepatocyte ... vacuolation of nuclei (glycogenic degradation)'. (Book p1014)

items.q: Match each hepatotoxin or metabolic disorder with the specific hepatic lobular zone it affects — 1) Paracetamol and ischemia 2) Yellow phosphorus 3) Wilson's disease … A) Zone 2 (midzonal) B) Zone 3 (centrilobular) C) Zone 1 (periportal)
items.exp: Zone involvement: Paracetamol is centrilobular (Zone 3), phosphorus is midzonal (Zone 2), and Wilson's disease affects periportal (Zone 1) hepatocytes. (Book p1014)

items.q: Besides hepatocytes, in which hepatic sinusoidal cell type does excess copper deposit in Wilson's disease?
items.exp: Histopathology notes: 'Cu2+ deposition inside Kuffer [Kupffer] cell.' (Book p1014)

items.q: How many years typically elapse before neurological manifestations emerge in Wilson's disease (Neuro-Wilson's)?
items.exp: Under Neuro-Wilson's, the text notes: '10 years for presentation.' (Book p1014)

items.q: Assess the two statements on Wilson's disease: I Steatosis (fatty liver-like change) is a recognized histological feature of both Hepatitis C and Wilson's disease. II Neurological Wilson's primarily involves the head of the caudate nucleus while sparing the lenticular nucleus.
items.exp: Statement I is true ('Steatosis: HCV & Wilson's disease'). Statement II is false because Neuro-Wilson's is hepatolenticular degeneration involving the lenticular nucleus. (Book p1014)
